source.title: Weak-Driven Learning: How Weak Agents make Strong Agents Stronger
source.authors: Ze-Hao Chen; Gong-Xun Li; Tian-Xiang Ai; Yi-Fei Li; Zi-Xuan Huang; Wang Zhou; Fu-Zhen Zhuang; Xiang-Long Liu; Jian-Xin Li; De-Qing Wang; Yikun Ban

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and evaluates its own weak-agent training method. It uses historical weak checkpoints as corrective signals, but does not test fine-tuning a strong model on labels produced by a weak supervisor or measure PGR.
record.gate_note: The paper’s intervention mixes weak and strong checkpoint logits and trains against ground-truth tokens; it is not weak-label supervision. Its benchmark comparisons do not establish that a student beats the weak supervisor or recovers a measured fraction of the weak-to-strong gap. The extracted results below describe this related alternative, not a tested claim version.
record.test_reason: The study trains a model with ground-truth cross-entropy on mixed logits from a historical weak checkpoint and the current strong checkpoint. No strong model is fine-tuned on weak-supervisor labels. No weak-supervisor or strong-ceiling comparison and no PGR is reported. All results compare the paper's own method (WMSS) against SFT and other post-training baselines, so the study does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that weak historical checkpoints can serve as corrective signal through weak-strong logit mixing anchored on ground truth. They find WMSS beats SFT and the baselines on math, code and logic. They also say the benefit needs enough weak-strong entropy separation, and that open-ended tasks are untested.
record.recipe_differences: The study mixes historical weak-checkpoint and current strong-checkpoint logits, then applies cross-entropy to ground-truth tokens; it does not fine-tune on weak-model-generated labels. It also uses entropy-based sample selection.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to the weak–strong entropy gap and to mixing coefficient λ; close checkpoint pairings can degrade results, and the λ sweep has a broad high-performing range around 0.42–0.50.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixing logits from a historical weak checkpoint with the current model's logits, under ground-truth cross-entropy, improves benchmark averages over two-epoch SFT. Math-Avg gains range from +2.9 to +5.9 across four 3B–8B bases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weak historical checkpoints used as a logit-mixing corrective signal (not as labels) can improve a strong model trained on gold labels.

record.problems: The authors describe the main comparisons as single-run comparisons and report no uncertainty estimates for them. The reported gains compare WMSS with SFT and other baselines, not with a weak supervisor or a strong true-label ceiling.
record.rows_left_out: Other per-benchmark scores in Tables 1, 4, and 5, plus module ablations and sensitivity results, are not included because they are WMSS-specific method comparisons or diagnostics rather than tests of the weak-label/PGR claim.

untested.parts: No strong model is trained on weak labels. No weak-supervisor, weak-to-strong student or strong-ceiling accuracies are reported, so PGR cannot be computed.
No auxiliary confidence loss, weak-ensemble or loss-variant comparison within weak-label training. Gains are measured over gold-label SFT, not as PGR.
No PGR is reported across supervisor or student sizes, or across tasks.
No tests of exploitation of the weak supervisor, distribution shift, or shared errors.
The theory concerns gradient amplification under mixed logits, not when a student must beat its supervisor.

record.verdict_notes: Despite the title, 'weak' here means an earlier checkpoint of the same model. Supervision is gold labels, so the weak-to-strong (weak-label) paradigm is not studied. Burns et al. is cited only in related work. Main comparisons are single-run; the lambda sweep uses three runs.

versions.untested_parts: No weak-supervisor label fine-tuning, weak-supervisor performance comparison, strong ceiling comparison, or PGR measurement.
Compares WMSS with SFT and other post-training baselines, but does not measure PGR or test the specified changes to weak-label fine-tuning.
Varies backbones and tasks for WMSS, but does not report PGR across supervisor/student sizes, task types, or representations.
Does not test weak-supervisor-checkable failures, distribution shift, or the effect of shared weak/strong errors on PGR.
Provides conditional analysis of its own mixed-logit mechanism, not theory establishing when a student must beat its weak supervisor.
No vision experiments; the reported experiments use language models on reasoning and code tasks.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B-Base
rows.operation_detail: WMSS trains with weak/strong mixed logits and ground-truth cross-entropy, with discrepancy-based sample selection.
rows.measure: pass@1 accuracy, Math-Avg gain over SFT
rows.note: The paper explicitly reports the SFT and WMSS Math-Avg values as 64.2% and 69.1%, respectively. This is evidence about WMSS, not PGR.
rows.check: Own-method-vs-baseline comparison (WMSS vs SFT), not a weak-to-strong measure. The 'observed' state is meaningless for any version.
